plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective drawing of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section, cut open so the reader faces the flat end of the ring. The gray body carries fine radial hatching across its curved upper surface, and the central hole opens through the middle. Across the top, four horizontal dimension arrows stack in registration with a dashed vertical center line: the longest reaches the outer wall and is labeled R2, the next reaches the inner wall and is labeled R1, a third labeled r ends partway out, and a short one labeled dr marks a narrow increment just beyond it. At the right edge a vertical bracket labeled h gives the height of the rectangular face. Inside that face, at radius r, a thin vertical strip of width dr is filled solid orange and tagged da by a curved leader. A red arrow labeled i curls onto the left end of the ring, and two blue curved arrows sweep along the lower body in the direction of the circulating field. Setting one narrow shaded strip against the full cross-section signals that the flux is built up by integrating such elements outward from R1 to R2, which is what the self-inductance calculation requires.

elements: partial toroid body (rectangular cross-section ring, ~300° arc) with the opening/gap facing the camera so the central hole is visible
flat rectangular cut end-face on the RIGHT end of the arc (the annulus rectangle we look into, inner edge R1, outer edge R2, height h)
flat rectangular cut end-face on the LEFT end of the arc
fine radial hatching lines covering the curved top surface of the toroid (many thin lines from inner to outer radius)
shaded inner cylindrical wall of the hole (darker gray)
vertical dashed center axis line through the toroid center
top dimension arrow R2 (longest, from center axis to outer wall) with label R2
top dimension arrow R1 (center axis to inner wall) with label R1
top dimension arrow r (center axis to current strip radius) with label r
short top dimension arrow dr marking the strip width just beyond r, with label dr
dashed vertical guide lines dropping from the R2, R1, r, dr arrowheads to the body
vertical bracket on the right labeled h spanning the height of the rectangular face
thin vertical orange strip of width dr at radius r inside the right rectangular face, tagged da by a curved leader arrow
red curved arrow labeled i curling onto the left end of the ring (current direction)
two blue curved arrows sweeping along the lower body indicating the circulating magnetic field direction
live numeric readout of B(r) and dPhi (and accumulated Phi when in integral mode)

interactions.label: Radius r
interactions.teaches: Dragging the orange da strip from R1 toward R2 shows B(r) = mu0*N*i/(2*pi*r) falling as 1/r, so each equal-width radial slice dPhi = B(r)*h*dr contributes a different (decreasing) amount of flux

interactions.label: Flux view
interactions.teaches: Switching to the accumulated view fills the swept region from R1 to the current r, revealing that the total flux Phi = (mu0*N*i*h/2*pi)*ln(r/R1) is built by summing dPhi over radius — the integral the self-inductance derivation requires

demo_steps.title: Slice near inner wall
demo_steps.narration: With r just above R1 the orange da strip sits at the inner edge where B(r) is largest, so this thin slice carries the most flux per unit dr.

demo_steps.title: Slice near outer wall
demo_steps.narration: Move the strip out to r near R2: same width dr and same height h, but B(r) has dropped as 1/r, so dPhi for this slice is noticeably smaller.

demo_steps.title: Accumulated flux
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to the accumulated view: the region from R1 to the current r fills in, showing the running integral Phi(r) growing logarithmically as slices are summed outward.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: inner radius R1 = 1.0, outer radius R2 = 1.6, rectangular face height h = 0.5 (so the cross-section rectangle is 0.6 wide x 0.5 tall). Build the toroid as a partial ring spanning ~300° with the gap/opening facing the camera (toward +Z / front) so the central hole reads open; the two flat rectangular end-faces sit at the left and right ends of the arc, the RIGHT one carrying the orange strip and the h bracket. +X is screen-right (radial outward on the right face), +Y screen-up (height h), +Z toward viewer. Radial hatching = ~60 thin dark-gray lines on the top curved surface running inner-to-outer. Orange strip = a thin box of width dr (~0.04) and height h placed on the right end-face at the current r, color #e8731a. Accumulated-integral fill = a translucent orange wedge/sector on the end-face spanning R1..r, color #f0a060 at ~0.5 opacity. Dimension arrows and dashed guides are screen-space overlays anchored to the projected center axis and the R1/R2/r/dr radii; h bracket on the right edge. Field/current arrows: red #cc2222 (i) at left end, blue #2a7fd4 along the bottom. Physics for readout: B(r) = mu0*N*i/(2*pi*r); dPhi = B(r)*h*dr; Phi(r) = (mu0*N*i*h/(2*pi))*ln(r/R1). Use N=200, i=1A for plausible numbers.
interactionPlan.notes: Construct the toroid body with a custom BufferGeometry (sweep a rectangle along a circular arc of ~300°) or a LatheGeometry segment; keep the two end caps as flat rectangles so the right cap can host the strip and the integral fill as coplanar overlay meshes offset slightly (+Z epsilon) to avoid z-fighting. Recompute the orange strip position, the dr arrow, the r arrow, the B(r)/dPhi readout, and (in integral mode) the swept-fill geometry reactively on every slider change. For the toggle, keep both the single-strip mesh and the accumulated-fill mesh in the scene and show/hide rather than rebuilding. Dimension arrows/labels are HTML/SVG overlays positioned by projecting the relevant world points each frame so they stay registered with the geometry.
